blogs.title: Beyond Tokens: Why Training LLMs is Too Hard at the Token Level
blogs.description: An accessible deep dive into the fundamental flaw of current RL algorithms like GRPO. We explain why calculating importance ratios for every single token causes 'model collapse' in large language models and how Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) shifts the focus to the entire response to create a stable, reliable training signal.

blogs.title: No More Routing Replay: How GSPO Simplifies MoE Training
blogs.description: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are notoriously difficult to train with RL due to unstable expert activation. Discover how GSPO fundamentally solves this by avoiding complex workarounds like 'Routing Replay,' allowing massive MoE architectures to scale efficiently without artificial constraints or extra memory overhead.

blogs.title: The Counter-Intuitive Paradox: Why Clipping More Tokens Leads to Better Results
blogs.description: In standard RL, clipping important data points is seen as wasteful. But our latest research reveals a surprising truth: GSPO clips entire sequences rather than individual tokens, and this conservative approach actually yields higher efficiency and performance. Learn how ignoring noisy gradient estimates helps the model learn faster and smarter.

blogs.title: Breaking the Hardware Barrier: Using Inference Engines for Reinforcement Learning
blogs.description: Reimagining RL infrastructure for large-scale models. Since GSPO relies on sequence-level likelihoods rather than precise token-by-token calculations, it is robust enough to use data computed by inference engines directly. Read about how this breakthrough eliminates expensive recomputation loops and paves the way for fully disaggregated training-inference frameworks.
